label: EXPERIMENTAL snowpack-structure prediction for expert decision support. Not an avalanche forecast, danger rating or operational guidance.
source: Avalanche Canada Mountain Information Network (public reports)

reports.title: Bow summit
reports.comment:
quick: Good skiing to be had, was taken advantage of by many in the day

Tree gullies and shoulder skied well, variable HS up to 50cm to be found, higher HS in sheltered areas.

Skiing between 2200 and 2400m was best, still need to watch for rocks

No test profile but a thin crust was observed 20-40cm down on solar slopes, nothing reactive here and snow above this was very low density, Fist hardne…

reports.title: Ice Fall next to Bow Falls
reports.comment:
quick: Big ice pillar fell on the north side of bow falls area. 

Bow falls seemeed to be climbable and thick at some areas.

Climbed some Wi3 ice to the right instead, was able to place blue screws at some places.

reports.title: Flower Stem Couloir and snowpack update
reports.comment:
quick: Went up to assess the snow conditions as the rat race has now begun. What we found was quite surprising!

On our way up the mellow slopes of the bow summit area, we were seeing lots of shrubbies and thin spots. As we approached the couloir, conditions started to appear deeper and more consolidated.

The couloir was great, but could use another storm as there are a couple pinch points that c…

reports.title: Early Season Reminder
reports.comment:
avalanche: Ski cut a size 1.5 wind slab up a pedal in Flower couloir today. Crown was roughly 40cm deep & 10m long, running around 115m. 
 Wind transport continued to be extremely evident throughout the day. Even with an early season rocky snowpack be mindful of wind deposited features.

reports.title: Bow Summit check in
reports.comment:
quick: Went for short walk today at bow summit, to have a peek at conditions and see if I remembered how to pizza. Very busy out there with tracks on anything close to covered. 1 party in the flower and plenty of tracks in the dog leg, we kept it mellow with a few laps on in the Christmas trees. 

Temps were hovering around 0 or just below, snowing S-1 for the few hours we were out with very limit…

reports.title: Bow summit wind slabs
reports.comment: quick: Stong south winds from yesterday produced soft winds slabs on alpine terrian west, south and east.  Lee NE and N and beneath ridges skied better. Slabs were not very reactive with no whumping or cracking or avalanches. Midpack was supportive.  -2 to -4 all way with light to mod SW winds.

reports.title: Close call on Dogleg
reports.comment: avalanche: Party of 2 went to ski Dogleg. About 30 cm of low-density fist snow was found on the fan and the bottom two-thirds of the dogleg couloir. At around 2480m the low-density powder changed to a wind slab. We stopped briefly to talk about turning around and remotely triggered a size 1 windslab around 8m above us. We were lucky enough to stay on our feet the whole time and everyone was ok.

reports.title: Bow Gullies
reports.comment:
quick: Conditions were much better than expected. Around 20-30cm powder in untouched areas after the weekend storm. Similar to previous MIN saying leeward slopes were best with North to NE aspects measuring about 60cm deep. Continual light snowing all day, probs 3-5cm while we were touring. No signs of instability.
Didn't go into the alpine because snow was best around and below treeline, very win…

reports.title: Jimmy Junior bowl
reports.comment:
quick: Good early season conditions in Jimmy Junior bowl today.

The approach up the creek is thin and bushy but works fine. Caution skiing down.

60-80 cm in the main bowl, generally strong for the Rockies early season with two buried weak layers. Snowpack test results showed sudden collapse failures near the base of the snowpack.

No new avalanches observed.

The most notable observation over th…

reports.title: Soft laps at Bow summit
reports.comment: quick: Surprisingly good conditions at Bow Summit. You could see rocks poking out on obvious boulder fields but on the usual ski slopes coverage was good. Snow was especially good in the trees but a bit wind affected (?) and firmer in the open. It was fairly windy in the alpine but without signs of wind transport. No slabs or whumps were encountered.

reports.title: OXO
reports.comment: quick: We were a group of five that  went up to OXO on Saturday Nov.23.  We didn’t notice an obvious track leading into OXO so created our own.  Apologies to those that followed if it wasn’t the correct way.  Snow coverage in the trees were minimal.  Lots of fallen trees, rocks, branches etc that wanted to grab your skis and poles.  The snow was better above treeline.  The Nov and October crust se…

reports.title: Bow Summit snowpack results.
reports.comment:
quick: Went to Bow Summit area to dig a snow profile. 
Targeting areas of concern that are fans below cliff bands to look for slab properties over the crust layer. 
The results are as follows. 
2470m NE 35deg HS 95cm
CTE (4) SC dn 80cm
CTM (15) SC dn 80cm
CTH (25) SC dn 80cm 
Wide range of results, snowpack right side up but reacting on the crust and facets. Season is still young and so is the sno…

reports.title: Jimmy Jr Bowl
reports.comment: quick: Great day! Snow was snow with ski penetration of about 15 cm. We did not see or feel any signs of instability.

reports.title: Bow summit slide
reports.comment: quick: Went for a tour to Bow Summit Saturday.  Rode the upper slope from the ridge and had a size 1 release send me for a ride. No injury, lost 1 ski (Scott superguide red/black).

reports.title: Bow Summit - wind transport
reports.comment: quick: Surprising amount of wind at Bow Summit today moving a lot of snow amd forming new wind slabs.

reports.title: Crystal ridge
reports.comment: quick: Took a gander up to the southren most point on crystal ridge. Even though the forecast called for overcast. Ended being a blue bird day with an inversion. Sat on top of the ridge in the sun wearing nothing but base layers comfortably while enjoying our lunch. Steeper  SW slopes exhibited signs of spring skiingby the afternoo , lots of pin wheeling. East aspects had good riding but with the …

reports.title: Bow Summit Area
reports.comment: quick: Good skiing on mellow terrain. Several other groups in the area. Coverage down low was better than expected (for November). Higher up: 40-60cm on leeward slopes and in low areas; 5-30cm on windward slopes and on more exposed ridges. Clear skies and sunny until mid day, however surface snow remained dry.

reports.title: Oxo Peak
reports.comment: quick: We ski toured up Oxo Peak, enjoying calm conditions throughout the trip. No wind slabs were felt underfoot. However, travel was rugged, with rocks, branches, and logs protruding from the snowpack. At 2,500m, the snowpack depth measured 90cm. A snow profile revealed a crust layer about 20 cm above the ground, likely the October crust. No avalanches were observed.

reports.title: C-Train
reports.comment: quick: Light spindrift down C-Train all day, building in the afternoon. Lake is almost frozen, no snow instabilities observed.

reports.title: West Nile
reports.comment: quick: We skied two laps in the West Nile area, with decent turns in the runout zone. There were many rocks lurking right beneath the surface, but being deliberate on where you turn allows one to avoid most of them. We stayed clear of the headwall, which was frequently sluffing throughout the day (mostly sz 1, 2x sz 2 LD); the avi debris on the fans would have made for poor skiing anyway with an u…

reports.title: Ridge behind Dolomite peak
reports.comment:
quick: Thick crusts in the alpine, very sun affected.
Small collections of wind pockets with nice snow.
Snow rather heavy.
We dug a pit and saw a weak layer around 30cm from the top of the snowpack. 
Slid with 25 taps and low energy

Saw a small skier triggered avalanche around here: 51.66372° N, 116.34908° W

around 20 tracks along this face and a medium sized avalanche at: 51.66789° N, 116.36372…

reports.title: Crystal Ridge
reports.comment: quick: Poked around Crystal Ridge area today, staying TL and below. Best snow was found in sheltered trees, 10-30cm unconsolidated powder on top of crust or firm mid pack depending on aspect. Wind effect was noted in open areas, with hand shears failing easy with 20-30cm wind slab. Had a few 1-2m wide slab releases around our turns in thin rocky areas, and very glad that we stayed away from anythi…

reports.title: Observation Sub-Peak
reports.comment: snowpack: Overall strong snowpack with CT 24 failing on deep layer (22cm from ground). HS was right around 70cm at tree line and riding quality was good although we didn't go too far into the alpine due to a party member getting sick.

reports.title: Mount Gordon
reports.comment: quick: Summited Mount Gordon from Bow lake (FYI follow shoreline where possible, some slush encountered). Broke trail; conditions marginal @ & below treeline (see pic), i.e. new bald spots on skins. Cruised quickly through the canyon - ice over the creek made sketchy bridges that held. Avoided overhead, lee features that appeared loaded on N/E aspects, and stayed on mellow slopes <30deg; no eviden…

reports.title: Jimmy Jr bowl
reports.comment: quick: Went for a poke around Jimmy Jr bowl. Skin track into the bowl was in good condition, pleasant skinning. Made for a slightly sporty exit. HS of 70 at the bottom of the bowl. Skied the east facing aspect of the bowl which was supportive with about 15 cm’s of fluff on top. Also skied the lower half of the north facing couloir far skiers right of the bowl. This was less supportive. Old wind sl…

reports.title: Dolomite Circuit
reports.comment:
quick: Skied the Dolomite Circuit today, generally good travel conditions. Still feels like early season. Skin track up Helen Creek was established and easy to follow with some willowbashing in the slide paths and an easy creek crossing. Once above treeline we found trail breaking to be reasonable with average ski pen of 10-20cm. 

On solar aspects around 2300-2400m we found the Dec 7 crust ~10cm …

reports.title: Jimmy Jr Bowl
reports.comment:
quick: Great day out at jimmy jr. Busy with lots of traffic but managed a lap down skiers right ish of the main bowl away from most of the skiers. Lap 2 we ventured into the north facing couloir mentioned in a MIN from Wednesday. Boot packed about 15m higher than the previous tracks. Found fantastic snow.

As mentioned in that Wednesday MIN we noticed the old windslab underneath the fresher snow w…

reports.title: West Nile
reports.comment: quick: Attempted West Nile. Skinned up to the slide path where the coverage became extremely poor, with exposed deadfall everywhere. The upper sections look like decent skiing but you have to brave a heinous bushwhack to get there right now.

reports.title: Busy day at Jimmy Junior
reports.comment:
quick: Quite a few parties up at Jimmy Junior bowl today, counted a little over 20 people. Ski quality good, with average 10cm of fist on top of a firmer supportive midpack. Snowed S-1 all day with wind transport intensifying throughout day, plenty of blowing snow off the headwall loading the top of the bowl. 

By the time we left around 1430 we noticed the newly transported snow was filling in pr…

reports.title: Where the Sidewalk Ends
reports.comment: avalanche: Wind slab avalanche that stepped down to the deep persistent layer. See incident report. / incident: Attempted to climb "Where the Sidewalk Ends." Skinned up the lower approach slopes south of the approach gulley and observed several shooting cracks propagating <1m. Upon transitioning into the steep gulley fan (~45 degrees), we observed a small settlement. Several minutes later, we trig…

reports.title: Dolomite Shoulder Partial burial
reports.comment: quick: Wumpfing and shooting cracks were witnessed on the top of the ridge as we ascended. We were planning on skiing out our uptrack but ended up attempting to ski cut a low angle run on an north east aspect off the lower part of the shoulder above treeline. The slope ripped to size 3 above the skier in their "safe zone" after the ski cut. The avalanche carried them ~300m to a partial burial.  Th…

reports.title: Bow Summit
reports.comment: quick: Super great riding for December. Lots of cross loading. Different areas had between 45 cm to 90 cm, but there were great powder pockets to be found.

reports.title: Dolomite
reports.comment:
quick: we skied off an unnamed ridge between dolomite and cirque right above katherine lake. noticed some whumpfs and shooting cracks on the uptrack and decided to ski a small mellow slope along the ridge. wind-affected and thin in some spots in the alpine; ok in the trees but still early-season conditions. 
observed a natural size 2 on the south ridge of cirque peak in steep terrain below ridge c…

reports.title: Crowfoot Glades
reports.comment:
quick: Amazing blue bird day in the glades. The soft powder was consistent throughout everywhere we skied. We did two laps of the glades, skiing slopes around 30 degrees. 

We observed two natural avalanches from the overhead hazard above. Neither was very large (we estimate size 1.5). One was observed from the car before going up, and the second when we were skinning near the top. They fell from …

reports.title: Bow Summit
reports.comment: quick: Thin layer of fresh windslab (up to 2cm) starting to crossload on some slopes, with considerable ongoing wind transport throughout day. <5cm of faceted snow noted at ground level, with the rest of the snowpack being generally cohesive and uniform in consistency. Snow conditions felt pretty stable, with a CT yielding no concerning results. Pockets of light powder still found in gladed areas …

reports.title: Granddaddy size 3+
reports.comment: avalanche: Granddaddy size 3+ natural ran the length of the couloir. No burials or humans in the fire line, unsure what triggered or failed. Photos screenshotted from video. Overcast and approx -4 temps, no notable wind or precipitation. Ran from what looked like the top of the couloir to the base of the fan/rock-piles.

reports.title: Cybertrucks on the parkway
reports.comment: quick: Skied Helen shoulder. Snow on the burnt trees side heading up lookers right towards the ridge was all facets and sugary snow that had no support and just sunk through every step with a slab underneath as we gained the ridge crest under the rocks. We followed the ridge lookers left (S/SE) and ended up on hard surface windslab that was hollow, and as we turned the corner headed E we heard 2 b…

reports.title: Bow Summit Size 2
reports.comment: avalanche: A relatively recent skier triggered avalanche judging by the skin track in the start zone. Looked to be an initial wind slab that stepped down to the persistent layer. Lots of wind loading visible at bow summit and the wind was continuing to blow snow around this morning.

reports.title: Crowfoot glades
reports.comment: quick: Great day in crowfoot glades. Saw some sluff coming off of overhead above (see picture), did not propagate below. Snow falling throughout the day, approximately 3 cm accumulation. Getting to be a little skied out but overall good skiing quality.

reports.title: Pac Man Bail
reports.comment: quick: sunrise pac man couloir attempt, coverage on the NE Aspect above the shoulder was terrible, we couldn't skin to the base of the couloir and tried to bootpack around and below the rock steps. About 50m below the couloir entrance we found a reactive 25cm wind slab, and bailed. the east facing slopes below the shoulder had 20cm new snow making for lovely riding - HS 60cm, so still ran into a f…

reports.title: Grand Daddy
reports.comment: quick: made it about halfway through the crux choke on grand daddy, then coverage got thin so we transitioned. bottom 2/3 of the couloir had small pockets of a slightly denser 20-30cm layer buried under 10-30cm of unconsolidated snow. Did not consistently fail on hand shears. observed small amounts of sluff coming off some of the walls lower down. also observed a skier triggered 0.5 avy in the pil…

reports.title: Crowfoot Glades AST 2 course
reports.comment: quick: Took Part in an AST 2 course day outing. Snow was weak and could punch through very easily. Did not see any natural avalanche activity except for dry loose sloughing off of the headwall.

reports.title: Sugar mountain
reports.comment:
snowpack: Isolated column/compression test showed failure at around 25cm on 3/4th full arm strike.

Top 25+cm of snow are extremely sugary (good riding) but are resting on a more consolidated layer.

Bottom of the snow pack appears extremely faceted.

reports.title: Sugar mountain
reports.comment:
snowpack: Isolated column/compression test showed failure at around 25cm on 3/4th full arm strike.

Top 25+cm of snow are extremely sugary (good riding) but are resting on a more consolidated layer.

Bottom of the snow pack appears extremely faceted.

reports.title: Grandaddy Couloir Cornice Fall
reports.comment: incident: Three climbers were transitioning around 25 meters from the top of Grandaddy Couloir when a portion of the cornice collapsed, triggering a size 1 avalanche at the top of the couloir. The avalanche swept over all three climbers; however, all individuals successfully self-arrested, and none were carried away. Member 1’s snowboard and Member 2’s bag were displaced by the slide. Member 2 des…

reports.title: Observation observation
reports.comment:
quick: Good skiing on shallow snowpack, with pockets of unsupported and a few sharks.  
2 tests:  
1) ECT at 2250 m (SW aspect, 20o): ECTX (plot provided here)
2) CT at 2400 m (SW aspect, 20o): CTM 14, sudden collapse down 25.

reports.title: Sugar Cube Couloir Quick Lap
reports.comment: quick: Quick boot up the Sugar Cube to the top of the cube, did not continue into the bowl above. Minor cross loading in fan below, observed shooting cracks propagating 5m off skis on lee features, snow was much more consistent on NE side. Average 20cm of F overlying approx. 60cm of 1F consolidated midpack on top of basal facets. Supportive midpack made for quick bootpacking and high quality skiin…

reports.title: Crowfoot Glades
reports.comment: quick: Consolidation of top layer led to some sinking from collapse of layer below. Active sluffs off of cliffs all day.

reports.title: Helen shoulder
reports.comment:
quick: -9C when we left the car at 10:00am, -5C at the car at 2:30.

Some thin spots near the rocks which we tried to avoid on our up track but downhill riding was surprisingly good. We skied near the burn and found below knee deep powder at times. 
Didn’t notice any signs of instability, or any activity out there. 

About 80cm HS at the top. Overall really good with less deadfall poking out than …

reports.title: Little Crowfoot
reports.comment:
quick: Skiied Little Crowfoot today. Good conditions and good skiing up high. Widespread surface hoar and surface facetting.  Snowpack was much thinner at lower elevations and became unsupportive on skis below ~ 2400m. 

Winds were picking up as we left ~ 1 pm.

reports.title: Crowfoot glades
reports.comment: quick: Started 9am, around -6 at the highway and no sign of wind. Snowing moderately all the way up to treeline, then tapered off around 11am but stayed cloudy. Observed multiple dry loose size 1s off the crowfoot mtn rock face. Temps around -4 at treeline. Skied a few laps and snow was good powder, supportive for skiing. Some tracks from the last few days looked to have filled in about 3-5cm new …

reports.title: Bow Summit skiing well
reports.comment: quick: Skied the far south bowl area of Bow Summit. There was 5-8 cm of fresh snow in the existing skin tracks. The bowl had areas that were a bit chunky from previous skiers but other areas skied well. Powder in the trees below the bowl was great. No evidence of avalanche activity or wind slabs.

reports.title: VariaBowl
reports.comment: quick: We skinned up the creek to Hidden Bowl. There were a couple other crews about. The skiing was quite variable in the bowl, could feel the wind affect and the snow was quite facetted. We crossed the lookers left avy path one at a time. The snow held, but we opted to ski out a different path.

reports.title: OXO Ramp
reports.comment: quick: Skied OXO Ramp. Conditions were stable but some wind slabs and crust areas. Skiing at the very top was crusty for 100m then soft and powdery below that until treeline. Skiing in the trees was also soft. Some sharky areas but overall good coverage where we chose to ski. Overall a great day out!

reports.title: Observation Peak Avalanche
reports.comment: avalanche: Slab failed sometime during the day, suspect solar triggered. It was hard to tell whether it was a windslab or a deep persistent slab, but notably the slab entrained facets and ran quite far given the size of the crown.

reports.title: Grand Daddy Couloir
reports.comment: quick: We tackled Grand Daddy Couloir for the first time. The snow in the couloir was quite hard, but once we hit the funnel, the snow was fantastic. We didn’t come across any weak layers and had no major concerns, aside from just making it down that steep monster in one piece! It was an epic day out there!

reports.title: Observation Sub Peak wind slabs
reports.comment: quick: Skied up to Observation Sub Peak. Ascended via the South east ridge. Through the trees and up to tree line the snow was unsupportive. Above treeline and in the Alpine was very wind affected. Snow was hard packed and crusty. Noticed a few shooting cracks going no more than 0.5m from you. Overall the windslab was unreactive. Found a few isolated pockets of good skiing from the top. / snowpack…

reports.title: Crowfoot Glacier
reports.comment:
quick: Date: Jan 19, 2025
Location: Crowfoot Glades


-20°C at 09:00 AM, calm in trees, signs of wind slab above 2,200 m.


Cracking observed near 2,200 m as we were skinning up.

We dug a snowpit at 2,150m (NE aspect).

Column tests failed at 40 cm (resistive planar, CP26-28).

No failure and no propagation in the extended column test.

Size 1.5 avalanche crown under Crowfoot Glacier at 51.64019,…

reports.title: Bow Summit Glades
reports.comment:
snowpack: Quick pit dug at top of main skin track en route to upper shoulder.  Three tests: 
CTE8,RP,down 20cm on windslab/PP interface
CTH27,SC, down 80cm on Basal facets
ECTX no-result

Variable surface during ski down from shoulder, mix of wind slab and powder on exposed SE aspect.

reports.title: Helen Rock Garden
reports.comment: weather: S-1 for 90min during skin up.  Light wind out of the North throughout. / snowpack: Surface was 1mm DF in lees where windslab wasn't present.

reports.title: Dolomite Circuit
reports.comment:
quick: The snow was heavily wind affected in most of the alpine with pocket of wind deposited power to be found on leeward slopes. No rocks were hit by our party but there are definitely rocks near surface which were hit with our poles while skinning.

One size 1.5 to 2 avalanche which was a few days old was observed a few hundred meters up slope of the skin track in the first slide path.

reports.title: Mosquito
reports.comment: quick: Alpine was rock hard and wind blasted. Treeline had some good snow but still pretty thin.

reports.title: GD
reports.comment:
quick: Surprisingly "good" conditions for GD yesterday. -18 @ the parking lot in the morning with considerable rise in temps with elevation and through the day ending at -7 at the car in the PM. Skies were clear and winds were calm to light all day. 

Most of the open alpine is wind hammered but areas of great skiing are still available on the right features and supportive TL and BTL. Couloir itse…

reports.title: St. Nic Circumnavigation
reports.comment: quick: Major widespread wind effect observed. Ok but still variable ski quality on the toe of Bow glacier mainly due to snow deposited via downflow winds. / avalanche: No naturals observed. 1 Skier triggered windslab size 1 occurred as the second skier in group was traversing above canyon to get into the canyon during exit. Isolated, stubborn. Ref last 3 photos

reports.title: Cirque Forepeak Wind Slab
reports.comment:
incident: Low doesn’t mean No avalanches.
And the snowpack is still made up of junk.

The day had been bluebird, mild temps with very little wind. Until a summit of Cirque peak where we experienced mod-strong winds in the afternoon.

Alpine conditions were highly variable with bulletproof wind hammered surfaces or rotten facet junk. Ski crampons would almost have made travel easier. Also noted a 2…

reports.title: Bow hut & Jimmy Jr
reports.comment:
quick: 2 nights at bow hut. 

On Wednesday winds were strong all day. Rough travel conditions, snow heavily wind scoured with lots of sastrugi and many rocks showings. Sheltered areas were faceted and unsupportive.

Probed average of 150cm on the toe of the glacier. Observed 2 windslabs on steep crossloaded southern alpine features entraining facets and running far. 

We abandoned plans for Mt Gor…

reports.title: Crowfoot area
reports.comment: quick: Crowfoot skied well on the north side. Quite deep powder with no wind affect or slab properties. Winds were very strong up high from a west sw direction, but it was quite calm sheltered behind Bowcrow peak.

reports.title: Dolomite shoulder
reports.comment:
quick: Started with -24 at the car at 8.45, big inversion (felt like negative single digit at 2300)

Not so much new snow down in the forest, about 10cm only. It’s sitting on unsupportive facets that makes poor riding quality as soon as you step out of the old tracks

Higher on the ridge there is more fresh snow (25-30cm) but it still sits on unsupportive facets. Couple of old tracks barely visibl…

reports.title: Helen shoulder sunshine
reports.comment: quick: After leaving the car at -26°c and snowing we were expecting a cold day. Pleasantly surprised as we broke through trees to sunshine and warner temps. Skied the south aspect of Helen's shoulder. Lots of whumfing and shooting cracks in any untouched terrain. Dug a quick pit and found 20cm of HST on top of a 3cm MFcr. All tests were failing on isolation below this crust 3mm near surface facets…

reports.title: mosquito creek
reports.comment: quick: went to try any ski ramp peak back behind oxo. -25 at the parking lot 8am then -11 or so end of day.  somewhat of an inversion it was warm and no wind up at tree line. Unfortunately turned around at the base of the ramp. It seemed there was 20-30 cm on top of a very slidy and very well defined layer which we found on multiple aspects. there were inconsistent points where shooting cracks wer…

reports.title: Bow Summit
reports.comment: quick: Overcast in morning until 12 pm, then sun appeared afternoon.  More clouds later after sun went behind the mountain.  Wind picked up after 2 pm. / snowpack: Performed exercise to build snow shelters as part of training course.  No specific tests for fracture were performed.  Excavation revealed no base, deep unconsolidated snowpack.

reports.title: Puzzle Peak area
reports.comment: quick: The ramp of puzzle peak was fairly wind affected but was stable and we didn't have any shooting cracks. To the left of the skin track there was two natural slides but we couldn't tell how old they were. The skin track to the ramp was pretty solid but up the ramp it was hidden with wind blown snow.

reports.title: Observation Sub Peak West
reports.comment:
quick: A great day up to observation sub peak west, followed the skin track through the forest then broke left and headed up the ridge. Skin track is well established until the bowl then we broke trail along the ridge. Anything on an east aspect is completely wind scoured and down to rock, but there is a good level of snow in the bowls and gullies. 

Some fair cornices (1-3m) building along the ri…

reports.title: Small slab avalanche on route to Bow Hut
reports.comment: avalanche: Our party traveled to Bow Hut on Saturday, February 15, returning the next day to the trailhead.  Between 11 am on Feb 15 and about the same time on Feb 16, a small avalanche released into the canyon on the main route to Bow Hut.  The avalanche occurred at the point where the path leaves the canyon on the path into the hut.  A member of our party had set a new skin track above the slide…

reports.title: Crowfoot glades
reports.comment:
quick: Followed the skin track across the lake and through the forest into the alpine
No significant cornices were observed overhead, but we observed a size 0/1 crown failure (about 10m across) in one of the fans above us on the climber's right so we just stayed within TL and BTL. 
Snow was deep in the trees and we had some amazing glade skiing, though there were small patches of crust skiing at T…

reports.title: West Nile
reports.comment:
quick: We went up West Nile today, leaving the trail in -17°C. By 3:30, it warmed to -5°C.

At treeline, a crust collapsed under our feet, so we dug a pit on the lee side of a wind slab.

Snowpack: 150 cm total. Top 40 cm was soft pow, then a hard crust (110–100 cm). Below 95 cm, faceted snow. In a column test, the 110 cm layer kept collapsing as we cut it. We turned around.

On the way down, we s…

reports.title: Jimmy Jr Bowl
reports.comment: quick: Some powder, some crust, and some parts of the bowl are getting pretty chopped up. Overall good skiing in the morning. / avalanche: Started out at 09:00 and made several laps without incident. Observed noticeable warming, slippery snow, and small pinwheels while ascending at around 12:15. Stopped at the top around 12:30 and noticed several wet point releases that must have happened during t…

reports.title: Wapta
reports.comment: quick: 3 days on the Wapta starting at Bow lake. Extremely windy on Sat above Bow Hut, not the best place to find some Pow turns with widespread wind affect on the glacier. Coverage on the glaciers was generally quite good. Only place we measured height of snow was on vulture Glacier with a 200cm snowpack. Travel was reasonably slow with the 25-30cms of consolidated snow providing too much resista…

reports.title: Little crowfoot
reports.comment:
quick: Skied little crowfoot today. Travel in canyon has improved in the last month. Still open water, thinner then normal. The snow ranged from powder to firm styrofoam on the moraines and powder on the glacier 

We probed 1.5m on the Ferris glacier.

reports.title: Observation Bench
reports.comment:
quick: Facets and crusts on more solar aspects. Deep facets and less crust in more protected areas that rode well.
Approx 70cm hs at treeline. Wind scoured alipne.

reports.title: Helen Shoulder - Slabs and Facets
reports.comment: quick: 3-5cm compact ice/crust layer on the surface in many areas at and below tree line. Underneath was all large facets with almost no support in most places. Ski pen was often knee deep once the crust gave way. Alpine and open areas were also quite wind affected with a few cm additional snow on top of the crust. Very slabby and difficult to move around.

reports.title: Dolomite Shoulder Remote Trigger
reports.comment:
quick: We had a great day on Dolomite Shoulder. Sportive crust with ~10cm on top in most places. Very faceted below the crust. Skiing the trees back to the road was pretty enjoyable with the refresh. See my other MIN from the day for more snowpack observations. 

We had a close remote trigger. While skiing down the SE ridge the NE wind loaded slope released and propagated up the ridge. No skiers w…

reports.title: Dolomite Shoulder
reports.comment:
snowpack: CT8 - BRK in FC ~ 45cm
ECTX

F to 4F new snow on top of K MFCr 15cm down
1F until K MFCr 25cm down
1F to F at base

reports.title: Crowfoot Glades
reports.comment: quick: New snow is very supportive overall, but sitting on large facets and a crust layer in many places. Steep scree slopes had several areas with decent sluffing, but no slab slides we could see. What sounded to be several larger slides from higher up to the north of crowfoot glacier could be heard however. Weather was a few degrees below zero with light flurries and wind gusts from the south.

reports.title: Tree triangle on Observation Peak
reports.comment:
quick: Wind up top on the ridges is picking up fresh 3-4cm of snow at a good clip, expect lots of transport. 
We climbed up the tree triangle, fresh 5-10cm of snow on top of a sun crust. 
Downhill turns did not punch thru the crust, very creamy, very dreamy. / weather: Wind up top on the ridges is picking up fresh 3-4cm of snow at a good clip, expect lots of transport. 
We climbed up the tree tria…

reports.title: Jimmy Junior
reports.comment:
quick: Did a few laps at Jimmy Junior bowl.

There were a few old size 1 avalanches covered by a light dusting of snow and one size 2 on the right side which seemed newer as it had no fresh snow on it.

The snow quality was excellent and we had some great turns.

reports.title: Bow Summit
reports.comment:
quick: Surprisingly great skiing today! / snowpack: CTH29 SP down 70cm
Facets for bottom 45cm to ground
Slope angle 28 degrees

Top 70cm well consolidated

reports.title: Flower / Bow Summit
reports.comment:
quick: Backed off flower couloir after punching through a variable wind slab. +Shooting cracks up to 2-3m wide at the bottom of Dogleg with blocks of up to 40-50cm, PWL.

Old avalanche debris was surprisingly easy to punch through as well.

reports.title: Jimmy jr
reports.comment: quick: Witness 3 class 0.5-1 avalanches release in a sun effected area when we where eating lunch.

reports.title: Tree line lap
reports.comment: quick: Was punching through the crust on every turn. Heard a large avalanche across the valley but couldn’t see it with the low cloud layer.

reports.title: Skier accidental size 2.5 on the Dolomite Traverse
reports.comment:
incident: The group was traversing a steep slope on the way to Dolomite Pass in poor visibility and off the regular route. The avalanche occurred as the second skier was crossing the slope.

The first skier was caught but only carried a short distance. The second skier was carried most of the way down the slope and fully buried. 

The buried skier was dug out by companion rescue after ~7 minutes w…

reports.title: Crowfoot Glades
reports.comment:
quick: When we drove on the road, we quickly realized that there was way more snow than forecasted. We decided to be even more conservative.

Temperatures were very consistent around -2 all afternoon.

It was SNOWING and we needed it! We decided to dig a pit and here is what we found: 

Snowpack: 
-Bottom to 80cm was pure facets.
-Various crusts between 80 to 95cm.
-Pow from 95 to 175cm (fluffier …

reports.title: Snow storm crystal ridge
reports.comment: quick: Poked around crystal ridge on Sunday, made it to about 2400m after lots of hard trail breaking. Noticeable drop in the stability of the snowpack at treeline. Whumpfing and breaking through the new snow onto the facets. At treeline hand shears revealed a clean crust under the storm snow.

reports.title: Hard work on the up and down
reports.comment: quick: Knew to hip deep snow on the uptrack; grateful to share the trailbreaking with another group. Hard to go anywhere but straight on the down unless you were hitting a steeper pitch. Great weather all day. Witnessed several whumpfs and played it conservatively all day.

reports.title: Michela Adrian
reports.comment: quick: Attempted to skin into the Bow Hut for the first night of the Bow-Yoho traverse. In the pinch on the way up a small slide went remotely and buried one person up to their waist. Strong snow looked to have slid on an ice layer. Not much loading at all noted at the time.. We turned around. Met a group coming out who reported many large slides on the way down from the hut.

reports.title: Bow Summit Study Plot
reports.comment: snowpack: The main concern in the snowpack is the very weak layer of facets from the January drought down about 85 cm. There has been lots of avalanche activity on this layer up to size 3.5 in the past 24 hrs, and it will likely remain a problem for the foreseeable future.

reports.title: Spicy on the Wapta
reports.comment: quick: Tried to head up to Bow Hut. Noticed s1-3 slab avalanches on all aspects. Significant wind transport as well as cohesion in the storm slab. Low vis and still stormy. Used test slope btl and triggered s1 with large propagation. Slide propagated 50m from original trigger point with a 50-80cm crown. Now would be a good time to go climbing :)

reports.title: Spicy on the Wapta
reports.comment: quick: Tried to head up to Bow Hut. Noticed s1-3 slab avalanches on all aspects. Significant wind transport as well as cohesion in the storm slab. Low vis and still stormy. Used test slope btl and triggered s1 with large propagation. Slide propagated 50m from original trigger point with a 50-80cm crown. Now would be a good time to go climbing :)

reports.title: size 3  + num sz2 - Observation Sub Peak
reports.comment: quick: Skier remoted a Size 3 from 1800m on Observation sub peak / avalanche: Regrouped on a ridge and felt a whumpf. Avalanche initiated in bowl feature and ran into gullies. First avalanche was a size 2 and then we saw a size 3 come out of another bowl feature. From the road we observed a 3rd size 2 that was triggered further around the ridge.

reports.title: OXO/Puzzle Failed Attempt
reports.comment:
quick: Whumpfing and cracking abundant once breaking trail. One crack travelled over 50m to the edge of a creek and let go a small slab. We never got above treeline because conditions were far too touchy and trail breaking was far too difficult. 

We viewed many several storm slab avalanches from the valley even with low visibility.

reports.title: Blower on Cirque Forepeak
reports.comment: quick: Amazing day out at Cirque Forepeak. Ski pen was 30cm in the trees. Loose, unconsolidated blower pow sitting on soft slab. Did not break through to facets. In the low alpine the wind affect was obvious. 5-15cm loose snow sitting on a harder wind slab. Turned around before hitting any of the steeper alpine slopes, doubt it would have been good skiing. Skied up to 30 degrees on small isolated …

reports.title: Crowfoot Glades skied well and provided example evidence.
reports.comment:
quick: Came across a very small isolated avalanche below a stand of trees. Looked to be a wind slab that was remote triggered by another skier’s up track - but that is my conclusion based on what I thought were faint shooting cracks seen as we ascended by it. 

Slide looked to be a good representative of the problem in the larger forecasting area. 

The rest of Crowfoot Glades skied well and we di…

reports.title: Bow Canyon
reports.comment: quick: Took a look, a few of the entrance slopes had slid, we stopped before the exit slot canyon slopes to discus’s turning around. 2x class 1-1.5 sympathetic avalanches happens when regrouping. The higher consequence terrain just beyond this point remains very suspect.

reports.title: Crowfoot Moraines avalanche
reports.comment: quick: Terrible ski conditions at Pulpit 1. 10~cm of fresh over a hard icy crust, that would often disappear and become unsupportive snow to ground(likely the micro affects of shade). Very hard to ski conditions. Our tracks had about 3cm on them by the time we got back to the car. Putting my big skis away for the season… / avalanche: While skiing low angle runs across the valley my partner and I w…

reports.title: Skier Remote leading to multiple sympathetic releases
reports.comment:
avalanche: Skier remote size 2 triggered from 24 deg terrain resulted in 6 additional sympathetic persistent and deep persistent slab releases.  4 size 2-2.5. 2 size 3-3.5. 
Weak layer failure traveled across alpine bowl feature covering a distance of ~800m.

reports.title: Bowcrow Peak
reports.comment: quick: -8 and and cool in the morning but warmed up when the sun came out and south to west aspects TL and below got moist. While skinning in undistributed areas we had some whumpfing but the snow was supportive and ski pen was never more than 25 cm but when you got out of your skis you sank to the bottom of the snow pack. Nobody was parked at bow and suspect nobody has made it into the hut recent…

reports.title: Crystal Ridge
reports.comment:
quick: Took the skis for a hike up Crystal ridge to check on conditions. With the reports of touchy conditions and wide propagations, we managed terrain carefully to keep away from steep slopes or overhead hazard.

Travel conditions pretty good, easy trail breaking with 10-20cm ski pen. Good ski quality, breakable crust forming on open solar aspects at treeline and below. Found storm snow settling…

reports.title: Observation Sub Peak
reports.comment: quick: Traveling up the drainage to Obersavation Sub Peak on the Icefield Parkway. We noticed an overhanging crown which likely had broken within the 24 hrs producing a large D2 avalanche below. We also noticed a collection of smaller avalanche which must have broken as a result of the over hanging crown. We did notice an older avalanche higher up on Observation Sub Peak, but we didn’t travel high…

reports.title: Bow Lake Shenanigans
reports.comment:
quick: Left the parking lot around 9am and headed towards Bow hut for a little getaway. We were optimistic about making it to our destination but knew full well that we would probably be turned around. 

 Started noticing signs of instability at the end of the lake as we experienced large areas of settlement creating massive whumps. We continued forward through the gravel flats experiencing more w…

reports.title: Bow Hut approach info
reports.comment:
quick: Parks Canada Visitor Safety staff were in the Bow Lake area on Tuesday to try and capture aerial images of the avalanche activity on the approach to Bow Hut. The visibility did not cooperate at the upper elevations, however, we were able to look at the avalanche activity lower down.
The attached image shows approximately what slid above the trees on the standard approach to Bow Canyon with …

reports.title: Peyto Hut Approach
reports.comment: quick: The first slope greater than 30 degrees that our group encountered on the approach to the Peyto Hut slid to the ground (SS-AS-R2-D1).  Rapid warming after a snowy and cloudy morning made for lots of natural avalanches in the mountains surrounding Peyto Lake.  Significant whumpfing and sudden collapses were experienced on flat terrain throughout the day.

reports.title: Crowfoot - Bow Lake
reports.comment: quick: Spent the day riding low angle slopes below treeline. 10cm of powder over a supportive crust made for easy travel and good skiing. Rapid warming during the afternoon saw multiple avalanches release off of the cliffs on Crowfoot Mountain, sizes 1-2

reports.title: Observation Treeline Test Profile
reports.comment:
snowpack: Dug at the last Christmas trees on west facing treeline knob of Observation peak- normally a very wind-scoured shallow spot.
Sun was out for the first time in days: 10-15cm of new snow quickly became moist  over the crusts formed following peak heat /rain on March 27th with the recent storms. Foot and ski pen is shallow above these crusts. 
Our tests all cut through the crusts. Somewhere…

reports.title: Rhonda
reports.comment: quick: Lots of people out skiing above Bow hut today (5-7 groups). Travel through the mousetrap felt reasonable as most of the slopes had previously run except for a couple slopes towards the end of the feature which we spaced out under or avoided. Average HS on the glacier was 280-3m where we probed. Skiing was mostly good but some wind effect towards the top of Rhonda. Had one Whumpf on the top …

reports.title: Crowfoot Pass
reports.comment: quick: Dug pit at 2265m elevation, 14.11hr, NW facing before the col.  Sunny conditions, approx -5C.  2m snow total.  0cm to ~50cm significantly faceted, basically junk sugar.  Rain crust just above at about 55cm that is very easy to break through when stepped on directly (we fell through when digging pit).  55cm to 165cm very consistent, consolidated and stable layer; very uniform.  170cm to 200 …

reports.title: Gordon
reports.comment:
quick: Busy up on the Wapta today. 

Good over night freeze. Temps were well into the positives by the time we returned to the parking lot around 1:00pm. 

Evidence of many slab avalanches from last 48 hours particularly on steep, rocky, unsupported terrain on all aspects. Some wind loading. 

Good skiing was found where the snow was cold. Sun effected aspects were starting to develop a crust and …

reports.title: Cirque West Ridge
reports.comment: quick: Approaching the saddle of Cirque North Bowl via the West ridge we got cliffed out while sidling around the subpeak. Stepping onto what looked like a stable snow slope off the smaller subcliff turned out to be a mistake. Good chance it extended into a cornice but wasnt observed from above. One person was on the structure when it failed. Large blocks of wet slab fractured and slid approx 100-…

reports.title: Reactive wet slab
reports.comment: avalanche: Size 1 on some wet facet almost to the ground happened just bellow view point as one member of the group was crossing the slope. We turned around !

reports.title: Bow Summit (N side Mt. Jimmy Simpson)
reports.comment: quick: Pit:  1226hr, elevation 2323m.  Pit facing E-NE.  Overcast skies.  A few passing wind gusts (maybe <15km/hr, at most?).  Total 80cm snow.  Solid ice-snow combination 0-20cm. No basal facets.  Weak snow layer at 20cm.  Ice layer at 50cm.  Fist penetrated easily at 60cm.  Ice layer at 65cm.  Unconsolidated snow between the 50cm and 60cm ice layers.  Fresh snow 66cm-80cm.  65cm ice layer caved…

reports.title: St Nicholas Remote
reports.comment: avalanche: Skied around the bow area today hoping for better vis. We were on plan C to see where we could get to on St Nic. We skinned along the upper bench, already deciding we were not going to ski the steeper slopes, but travel as far as we could towards the summit. Hand shears showed moderate planer results of the 4F windslab 40cm deep on a 2cm crust, confirming our decision to not ski the slo…

reports.title: Bow-Yo April 7-11
reports.comment:
quick: Bow-Yo. April 7-11

Good conditions from Bow Lake to Stanley Mitchell Hut. Crevasses generally well-bridged. Ski pen only 10-15cm on most terrain. 3m+ HS at high point above Collie crevasse field. We encountered wind slab in some lee areas, particularly where you leave the Yoho Glacier to access the ridge to Guy Hut where we released a small slab of storm snow. Isolated Col was in good shap…

reports.title: Wind slabs are still out there!
reports.comment: quick: Very good ski quality on high alpine north aspects with 10-30 cm of low density powder increasing with elevation. / avalanche: Skinning up low angle <25* slope nearing the ridge crest. Settlement triggered steep wind loaded pocket 50 metres away. 20 cm of new low density storm snow overlying 40 cm of soft windslab.

reports.title: Cirque Forepeak
reports.comment:
quick: We chose to try this because of the bomber crusts we'd seen and heard of in the area – despite S, SE aspects.

-11ºC in the parking lot at 8 AM. Went up the middle of the drainages and got out of the trees quickly through the northern gully marked on our maps. Saw a sz 1 natural from a few days ago. Once near treeline, skins slid on S aspect crusts so we stuck to N aspects.

Crust and ~10 c…

reports.title: Wapta in great shape
reports.comment:
quick: Great conditions up on the Wapta
Bow canyon is still in great shape
Bow lake still well frozen 
Lots of groups out
Thompson has snow on it!
Rhonda in great shape
Olive & Gordon still in great shape (skied them last weekend)
Still cold up on the Wapta in the wind, only evidence of sun effect was in the ski down from the hut
Great turns to be had on the Headwall

reports.title: St Nicholas
reports.comment:
quick: Nice conditions on the ridge of St Nicholas for bootpacking this morning. Snowpack was supportive underfoot. On the way down, the steeper slopes were wind-affected and skiing was grabby. Better turns on the mellower slopes. 
On Sunday, the wind was gusting at ridgetop, we were mindful of windslab during the trip.

reports.title: Slim Jimmy
reports.comment:
quick: Skied Mount Jimmy Simpson today. The day was mostly cloudy with steady winds keeping the snow cool. Solid crust up to the top of treeline on all solar slopes we travelled. In the alpine on more easterly aspects the crust became only a few cm’s thin and very breakable and hooky. 

A hasty pit showed several crusts in the upper 50 with the surface crust being not well bonded but having no ene…

reports.title: Dolomite Circuit
reports.comment:
quick: Went for a quick lap of Dolomite Circuit today. Temps were -8 at the car around 0700 when we started and +5 at the car at 1100 when we finished. In the alpine it was warm in the sun, though it didnt feel like ambient air temps went above zero while we were up there. We also observed light winds.

There was a solid melt/freeze crust on most aspects that we travelled on which made for fast tr…

reports.title: Crowfoot / Little Crowfoot / Ferris Glacier
reports.comment:
quick: Toured up to the summit of Crowfoot Mountain (and partway up Little Crowfoot). 

 Travel was fast and firm in the morning. Coverage in the canyon was good. No visible sags in the Ferris glacier. Skinned to the Crowfoot ridge line. A party of three ahead of us noted several settlements as they approached ridge line. We boot hiked/traversed to the true summit, keeping to areas of exposed rock…

reports.title: Granddaddy goes…
reports.comment:
quick: Skied the Granddaddy this morning.
Ski conditions were not great, but expected for the spring we are having. In the couloir itself it was dust on crust and bumpy, the fan skied a bit better. Below TL it was a breakable crust that was supportive if you skied slowly, a real turn often broke through. At approximately 1100 on the way out the storm came a few hours early and the walls started to…

reports.title: Crystal Ridge
reports.comment:
quick: Late afternoon tour up Crystal ridge via the western slopes. Crust held up remarkably well and was supportive corn skiing right to the car at 4pm. Moist surface snow everywhere I traveled except the summit ridge where the wind was able to keep the snow dry and the crust extra crusty. I was unable to get snow entraining on 35 degree SW slopes at treeline.

Blowing snow at ridgetop forming so…

reports.title: Mount Gordon
reports.comment:
quick: A solid overnight freeze made for quick travel up to Bow Hut. The snow/ice bridges in the canyon were still holding (although a few are getting slim). No obvious loose wet debris from yesterday below the Vulture/St. Nicholas wall. 

Conditions were refrozen on the glacier access ramp, becoming ~5cm dry powder on the glacier. Consistently probed >2m snow depth on the Mount Gordon approach. S…

reports.title: Little crowfoot
reports.comment: quick: No freeze below 2200m and partial above. Good travel on bow lake. Bow canyon was isothermic at the end of the day and a few snow bridges collapsed but travel is still easy just have to take your skis off a couple times.  West aspects were isothermic in the afternoon below 2400m. A few cm of convective flurries turned to glue when the sun came out. Above 2400m true north shaded still had som…

reports.title: Pick your perfection.
reports.comment: quick: Back from a summit bagging trip on the Wapta. Peyto approach was great on Thursday with fast travel conditions all the way to the hut. With the warm weather over the weekend I expect this approach will be a little more challenging but still doable. We exited out via Bow lake early Sunday morning and with a poor refreeze overnight found travel becoming increasingly difficult with loss of ele…

reports.title: GD
reports.comment: quick: Cornice collapse/fall at 8am from the climber’s left wall about 100m from the top.

reports.title: Ramp and Quartzite Corn Fest
reports.comment:
quick: Great day out in the Ramp peak area. Started very early before 6am to reach the top of Quartzite before noon. 

Noted the usual cornice collapse happening across the valley on south east aspects, and later on south aspects. No signs of weakening on the aspects we were on or travelling under. 

Once back to treeline, snow quality had deteriorated significantly, creating challenging condition…

reports.title: Watermelon Peak
reports.comment: quick: Good freeze made for a supportive approach on old tracks. Good travel and supportive freeze in the alpine all day. North aspects softened a little bit for decent corn skiing. Isothermic surviver skiing/ patch skiing on the exit below 2300m in the trees. Whumfing on flat areas in the alpine. Probed 300cm + on the glacier.
